$comment: CATiB trees for the tier-1 eval sentences — the input side of arc normalization. First derived by hand from Habash, Faraj & Roth 2009 (Syntactic Annotation in the Columbia Arabic Treebank), then VERIFIED against real output from CAMeL-Lab/camelbert-catib-parser: every head matched, and the labels are now the model's own. `head` is the id of the governing token, 0 for the root, matching the eval set and Parse.heads. A root carries the label `---`, which is what the model emits there — the guidelines describe `---` as the flat relation, but the CoNLL encoding reuses it for a token with no governor. Inserted covert pronouns are absent by construction: no parser emits them, and insertion runs after this stage.

source.citation: Habash, Faraj & Roth 2009, Syntactic Annotation in the Columbia Arabic Treebank
source.also: Habash & Roth 2009, CATiB: The Columbia Arabic Treebank, https://aclanthology.org/P09-2056.pdf

pos_tags.NOM: all nominals — nouns, adjectives, adverbs, pronouns, numbers; also preposition-like nouns such as فوق
pos_tags.PRT: all particles — prepositions, conjunctions, إنّ وأخواتها, negation particles

relations.SBJ: explicit subject of a verb (active or passive), and the subject of a nominal sentence including those headed by كان وأخواتها or إنّ وأخواتها
relations.OBJ: object of a verb, deverbal noun, or preposition; also children of coordinating and subordinating conjunctions
relations.PRD: predicate — only the complement of كان وأخواتها and إنّ وأخواتها
relations.TPC: topic of a complex nominal sentence whose complement has a different subject, typically with a resumptive pronoun
relations.IDF: the possessor in an idafa, and the object of a preposition-like nominal adverb
relations.TMZ: the specifier in a tamyiz construction
relations.MOD: general modifier — adjectival, adverbial, prepositional-phrase, and verbal particles such as لم
relations.---: flat — multi-word structures no other relation explains, e.g. parts of a proper name

trees.notes: Verb-initial, so CATiB and i'rab already agree. Re-rooting is a no-op.
Aspect does not change tree shape in CATiB either. CATiB has one VRB tag for both aspects.

The one place the model disagrees with the guidelines, and it is right to. The guidelines say 'For passive verbs (VRB-PASS), SBJ is the surface subject', which would make المقالة SBJ. The model emits OBJ, because undiacritized كتبت reads just as easily as active كَتَبَت 'she wrote' with a covert agent — and CAMeL ranks that active reading first too. The head is 0,1 either way, so normalization is untouched; only the label moves, and نائب فاعل vs مفعول به was always the rule engine's call off voice.
Guidelines: 'the verbless complement/predicate (الخبر) heads the topic/subject (المبتدأ)'. i'rab roots at المبتدأ, so this arc is the one that moves.

'The predicate of a nominal sentence can also be a preposition' — so the preposition roots the sentence. It already heads its object, which is the arc UD would invert and CATiB does not. Only the root moves.
CATiB has no adverb tag: 'Preposition-like nouns/adverbs such as أمام and فوق are considered NOMs', and 'idafa is also used to mark the objects of preposition-like nominal adverbs'.

SBJ not TPC: the topic 'is marked as SBJ if it is the same as the subject inside the complement; otherwise TPC'. Here it is the same. CATiB gives this the same tree as verb-initial 1(a) — i'rab does not, and word order is what separates them. Three tokens here, four in gold: the covert فاعل is inserted downstream.
'the topic/subject and complement/predicate are considered children of the incomplete verb with the relations SBJ and PRD'. Already i'rab-shaped.

'The same happens when a verb-like particle (إنّ وأخواتها) precedes the nominal sentence.' PADT attaches the topic under the predicate (I3rab Fig 11); CATiB agrees with i'rab instead, so nothing flips.

'A variety of particles can modify verbs' tense, polarity and aspect. These particles always attach under the verb with the relation MOD.' Same as PADT/UD; i'rab inverts it (I3rab Fig 16), which is exactly what re-rooting does.
Same shape as لم — both are negation particles under the guidelines' PRT. The جازم/ناصب distinction is mood, which no arc records.
IDF already runs possessor to possessed, so المضاف إليه hangs off المضاف and needs no flip. The root sits two arcs from token 1, so re-rooting reverses a path of length two.
'The most basic use of MOD is to mark adjectival modification.' Both adjectives are NOM, and the صفة/خبر split is definiteness — invisible to the parser, and the rule engine's problem.
